newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Mandela, Chiluba discuss Zambia deadlock solution.
newsitem.headline: Mandela, Chiluba discuss Zambia deadlock solution.

text.p: South African President Nelson Mandela met Zambian President Frederick Chiluba on Tuesday to discuss a compromise aimed at resolving Zambia's electoral impasse.

Mandela told a news conference after their hour-long meeting that Chiluba had put forth a "very important" proposal which could end an opposition party boycott of general elections scheduled for November 18.
"I am satisfied with our discussions and I am satisfied that we have made good progress which can bring about a solution in Zambia in regard to these elections," Mandela told reporters.

Chiluba, standing beside Mandela on the steps of the South African leader's residence, said: "I believe we will resolve this problem one way or the other...I came to consult and I believe that the discussions have been very well conducted."

Seven opposition parties, including former president Kenneth Kaunda's United National Independence Party, are boycotting the polls which they say have been arranged to ensure that Chiluba's Movement for Multi-party Democracy (MMD) remains in power.
The parties are opposed to a new constitution which bars some candidates, including Kaunda, from standing for president if they are first-generation Zambians.

Mandela declined to outline Chiluba's offer, saying: "What we are interested in is a settlement. (Chiluba) is a man with a great deal of responsibility and any suggestion he makes to me, he must canvass with his colleagues back in Zambia."
Asked if Monday's polls would go ahead on schedule, Chiluba left the door open for a possible postponement, saying: "For now I would say 'yes', but let's see if we can consult."

Lusaka's Suprme Court is expected to rule on on Wednesday on a petition by opposition parties challenging Chiluba's eligibility to contest the polls by alleging he lied about his parentage and nationality in filing nomination papers.
